papers.title: A Note on Carmichael Numbers of the form $ N=(d+1)(3d+1)(4d+1)$
papers.abstract: We study integers of the form \[ N=(d+1)(3d+1)(4d+1). \] Using Korselt's criterion, we prove that, provided the three factors are prime, $N$ is a Carmichael number if and only if \[ d\equiv4\pmod{12}. \] We also show that the special case $d=2^m$ produces only $1105$ under the prime-factor hypothesis.

papers.title: Riemannian Submersion whose Total Manifold admits an Almost Hyperbolic Ricci Soliton
papers.abstract: In the present paper, we investigate geometric properties of a Riemannian submersion for which the total manifold is endowed with hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons. We establish conditions under which the fibers of the submersion admit hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons. Further, we derive necessary conditions for the base manifold to be an Einstein and a hyperbolic Ricci soliton. Also, we determine the scalar curvature associated with the fibers and the base manifold. Moreover, when the total space admits an almost hyperbolic Ricci soliton with a torse-forming potential vector field, we obtain conditions ensuring that the extrinsic vertical and horizontal distributions are almost generalized quasi-Einstein. We also obtain necessary conditions for the fibers and base manifold to be an Einstein and almost generalized quasi-Einstein manifold. Finally, examples are included to illustrate the existence of hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons in Riemannian submersion.

papers.title: Irreducibility of the Cuboid Polynomial $Q_{p,q}(t)$ via the Rank-One Chabauty-Coleman Method
papers.abstract: Let $Q_{p,q}(t)\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be Sharipov's even monic degree-$10$ second cuboid polynomial, with coprime positive integers $p\ne q$. We prove that $Q_{p,q}(t)$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$, and hence over $\mathbb{Z}$. More generally, the normalized associated quintic $P_s(x)$ and its composition $P_s(t^2)$ are irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$ for every $s\in\mathbb{Q}\setminus\{0,\pm1\}$. The proof reduces linear and quadratic factors to rational points and horizontal conjugate pairs on one fixed genus-$2$ curve. A certified rank upper bound for its Jacobian, together with an exact divisor calculation, gives a rank-one annihilating differential at the prime $3$. For the quadratic-factor case, the symmetric coordinates of a horizontal pair lie on an explicit double cover of an elliptic quartic. All rational affine points on this model are $3$-adically integral and reduce to six smooth residue classes. The pulled-back differential is a unit in each class, proving that six displayed points form the complete list. Their coordinates exclude every admissible parameter. A negative real root of the irreducible quintic then supplies the additional degree argument required for irreducibility of the degree-$10$ polynomial. The rank computation and all exact arithmetic certificates are specified explicitly for reproduction.

papers.title: Prescribed Primitive Roots And The Least Primes
papers.abstract: Let $q\ne \pm1,v^2$ be a fixed integer. The least prime number $p \geq2 $ such that $q$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ is conjectured to be $p\ll (\log q)(\log \log q)),$ where $\gcd(p,q)=1$. This note proves the existence of a small subset of primes $p$ that satisfies the stated upper bound.

papers.title: On transcendence of non-periodic continued fractions associated with modular forms and arithmetic functions
papers.abstract: The purpose of this article is two-folds. Firstly, we establish two sufficient conditions under which the sequence $\{f(n)\pmod{m}: n\geq1\}$ is non-periodic, where $f(n)$ is an arithmetic function. As consequences, we deduce that the sequences associated with the Ramanujan tau function $\tau(n)$ as well as the Fourier coefficients of certain normalized Eisenstein series $E_k(z)$ modulo $m$ are non-periodic. Further, we deduce that the sequence arising from Nathanson's totient function $\Phi(n)$, the classical Euler's totient function $\varphi(n)$, sum of divisor function $\sigma(n)$, their Dirichlet convolution $\sigma*\varphi(n)$, Jordan's totient function $J_k(n)$, and unitary totient function $\varphi^*(n)$ modulo $m$, are non-periodic for certain modulo $m$. In addition, we extend a result of Ayad and Kihel \cite{r1} on the non-periodicity of certain arithmetic function $g(n)$. On the other hand, we construct several transcendental numbers arising from the continued fractions attached with $\tau(n)$, $E_k(z)$, $\Phi(n)$, $g(n)$, $\varphi(n)$, $\sigma(n)$, $\sigma*\varphi(n)$, $J_k(n)$, and $\varphi^*(n)$.

papers.title: Toward an exotic $S^2\times S^2$ and an exotic $\mathbb{CP}^2\#\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^2$
papers.abstract: We study a specified Luttinger filling in the construction of Lidman and Piccirillo whose simple connectivity would yield exotic $S^2\times S^2$ and $\mathbb{CP}^2\#\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^2$. An earlier version of this manuscript claimed simple connectivity from incorrectly derived group relations; that claim is withdrawn. We derive the complete fundamental-group presentation and express the group as a one-relator quotient of an iterated HNN extension containing the genus-two surface group. The filled group is trivial exactly when the final relation kills a specified fiber commutator. We also determine its universal central extension with cyclic kernel, construct geometric realizations of it, and extend the boundary involution over the filling. The final filling problem remains unresolved.

papers.title: Lateral Weak Stieltjes Derivatives: A Global Characterization of Stieltjes--Sobolev Spaces
papers.abstract: Weak formulations for Stieltjes differential equations must retain the directional information carried by atoms of the driving measure. We derive a lateral integration-by-parts identity in which the posterior trace of the test function is forced by the atomic product rule. The resulting dual formulation gives an exact global characterization of integral Stieltjes--Sobolev spaces for the full exponent range from one to infinity and reconstructs the unique strong representative from its traced weak state. We prove that the associated traced weak operator is closed, establish Poincar\'e--Stieltjes estimates, and \rev{characterize Stieltjes absolute continuity inside bounded variation through a canonical derivative measure whose restriction to the open interval is the classical distributional derivative}. The framework is then applied to finite-dimensional nonlinear measure-driven systems, yielding equivalence of weak, integral, and measure formulations, existence and uniqueness under integrable Lipschitz assumptions, compactness-based existence, and intrinsic reset laws. Cubic and logistic models illustrate the simultaneous encoding of continuous evolution and instantaneous interventions.

papers.title: Admissible $qx+1$ Sequences, Semiconvergents, and Rational Catalan Numbers
papers.abstract: Let $q\geq3$ be odd and put $m_r=\lfloor r\log_2q\rfloor$. We count parity sequences with exactly $r$ odd entries for which the coefficient in the $qx+1$ iteration first drops below $1$ at step $m_r+1$. Their number $a_q(r)$ also counts the corresponding residue classes modulo $2^{m_r+1}$. We derive a first-violation recurrence which, for $q=3$, proves a recurrence conjectured in 2015. We establish the sharp inequalities \[ \frac1r\binom{m_r-1}{r-1}\leq a_q(r)\leq\frac1r\binom{m_r}{r-1}. \] Equality is characterized by the lower and upper record indices of $\{r\log_2q\}$, equivalently by denominators of convergents and semiconvergents from below and above. At these indices $r\geq2$, the values $a_q(r)$ are rational Catalan numbers. We also characterize the dependence on $q$ and prove, for each fixed odd $q\geq3$, that $a_q(r)=\Theta_q(r^{-3/2}B_q^r)$, where $B_q=(\log_2q)^{\log_2q}/(\log_2q-1)^{\log_2q-1}$. For $q=3$, this settles Hikawa's conjecture concerning the polynomial factor in a related counting function.
